clue.text: Brisk look about a game

indicators.note: about means the word for look goes round the card game

parts.note: to spy is to look, to catch sight of
nap is a card game, short for napoleon

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick, lively glance around a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a brisk manner is quick and lively, as in 'make it brisk'.

clue.text: A lad required to gut fish

parts.note: to gut a building is to strip it of its insides
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A boy is needed in the kitchen to clean out the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gut fish' reads as one kitchen job, but the two words are separate pieces; 'required to' only joins the definition to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old word for a youth not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Star workers are given accommodation

indicators.note: given accommodation means the word are is housed inside the workers

parts.note: worker ants are the crossword's usual workers
taken as written

explanation.surface: The leading employees are provided with somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the red supergiant that is the brightest in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Long drinks incorporating very soft fruit

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: incorporating means the drinks take the musical marking inside them

parts.note: ales are beers, so drinks
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Tall cocktails are served with squashy bits of produce mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long drinks' reads as one phrase, but Long is a verb here and only the drinks do the 'incorporating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples: tropical produce with spiky leaves and yellow flesh; the plural matches the collective noun.

clue.text: Main race possibly in the United States

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The biggest sporting contest may well be held across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose adjectival sense: something found or made in that country is described by this word.

clue.text: People of note!

parts.note: note is read as a musical note rather than as distinction, so these are people who deal in notes

explanation.definitionFit: Pun: players and singers work with notes, though the phrase normally means the eminent.

clue.text: Bring up the right 'to a listening device

indicators.note: to says the first piece is placed next to the second

parts.note: the ear is the organ we listen with, whimsically a device

explanation.surface: Someone raises their entitlement to plant a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to raise children or animals.

clue.text: Are able to dance, but only for a spell

parts.note: you can means you are able
to trip is to dance with light steps, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: Some people manage a turn on the floor, though not for long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a spell' reads as a short while; here the spell is a witch's. 'but only for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a Scots word for a magic charm or a mischievous trick.

clue.text: A fellow climbing with 4 in a difficult situation

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the fellow is read upwards

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
the answer at 4 across describes things of the US

explanation.surface: A man goes up a mountain with three companions and finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns DON into NOD. The 4 is a cross-reference to 4 across, not a number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a knotty point, a complication, from the Latin for knot.

clue.text: Holiday charge around the end of August

indicators.note: around means the charge goes round the single letter

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: the end of asks for the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: A summer getaway costs extra in the last days of the school break.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a festival or feast day, a day off for celebration.

clue.text: Train and back oriental group with little hesitation

indicators.note: back means the whole run of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: E for eastern, which is what oriental means
a unit is a group, as in an army unit
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: After a slight pause someone coaches and supports a team from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb, to coach, but it is a noun: the attendants following a great person. One signal, 'back', covers all three pieces at once, so the hesitation ends up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the body of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Rushed around a woman, so got across

indicators.note: around means the word for rushed goes round the name

parts.note: sped is the past tense of speed, rushed
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone dashed past a lady and so reached the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bridge that reached from one side to the other did this.

clue.text: Endurance shown by individual in French church

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a man is an individual, a person
en is the French word for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: One worshipper in a Paris cathedral shows remarkable staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French church' reads as a place, but 'in French' is one piece and church another; 'by' also gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the quality of lasting, of continuing without end.

clue.text: A colourful setting for any pupil

definitions.text: A colourful setting for any pupil

parts.words: A colourful setting for any pupil
parts.note: the pupil is the dark opening of the eye, not a schoolchild, and its setting is the coloured ring round it

explanation.surface: A brightly decorated classroom suits every schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun on anatomy: the coloured ring of the eye surrounds the dark opening at its centre.

clue.text: Nice garden created by a younger relative

indicators.note: created says the letters before it are made into something new

explanation.surface: A lovely plot of flowers was laid out by a junior member of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the daughter of a nephew, two generations below.

clue.text: Empty flat

definitions.meaning: empty in the sense of lacking substance or interest, as of empty talk
flat in the sense of tasteless or dull, like a drink that has lost its sparkle

explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe something lacking flavour, life or interest.

clue.text: The underworld, being on the level, scoffed — so incongruous

parts.note: Dis is a Roman name for the underworld and its god
par is level, as in on a par with
to scoff food is to eat it, so scoffed is ate

explanation.surface: Gangland, finding itself going straight, jeered at how out of place that was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' reads as jeered; it means ate. 'being' and 'so' only join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things that do not match or belong together are essentially different in kind.

clue.text: A bolster the ordinary seaman finds quite suitable

parts.note: to bolster something is to prop it up
OS is the naval abbreviation for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor of the lowest rank thinks a long pillow just right for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolster' reads as a pillow; here it is the verb, to support. 'finds' joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a remark that is to the point is fitting and pertinent.

clue.text: Rack for supporting a casualty

definitions.meaning: the rack was an instrument of torture that pulled the body out lengthwise
a frame of poles and canvas is used for carrying an injured person

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a torture frame pulls limbs longer, and ambulance crews carry the injured on a litter of this name.

clue.text: Fish catches shown in stones

parts.note: the gar is a long-jawed fish
to net something is to catch it, so catches is nets

explanation.surface: An angler's haul is displayed lying on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish catches' reads as one phrase, an angler's haul, but it is two pieces. 'shown in' joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples: deep red gems used in jewellery.

clue.text: There's some purpose in ripped clothing …

indicators.note: in means the word for purpose sits inside the word for ripped

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, torn
an aim is a purpose, a goal

explanation.surface: Someone has a reason for wearing torn garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old or literary word for garments.

clue.text: Check sailors on the 'way back are more cheerful

indicators.note: back means the check and the sailors together are read from right to left

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
the NUS was the National Union of Seamen, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Inspect the crew returning home and you find them in better spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as an instruction to inspect; it is a restraint. One signal, 'back', covers both pieces at once, so the sailors, the old British seamen's union, end up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brighter, happier disposition, in the comparative.

clue.text: … to repeat, there's a point in ragged attire

indicators.note: in means the compass point is put inside the rearranged word
ragged clothes are torn to pieces, so the letters of the next word are broken up

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the last clue, there is some sense in wearing tattered clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' makes ITERAT from attire, and 'in' puts E inside it. The dots only tie the surface to the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to say or do something again.

clue.text: Hard cash!

parts.note: hard is taken literally: money in the form of solid metal rather than notes or credit

explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: metal money is physically solid, unlike paper notes.

clue.text: Figure on a Shakespearean role, being free

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a figure
Lear is the title part in Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.surface: An actor with a fine physique takes a part in the Bard without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a body or a person; it is a number, the Roman 100. 'being' joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a road with no obstruction is open and unblocked.

clue.text: The grouch, in other words, cannot melt

indicators.note: in other words says the letters can be put together as different words

explanation.surface: To put it another way, the grumbler has a heart that will not thaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a discontented person who is always complaining.

clue.text: The ship's company sounded exultant

definitions.meaning: the people who man a vessel
the old past tense of crow, to make a triumphant cry like a cockerel

explanation.surface: Everyone aboard the vessel cheered in triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the hands aboard a vessel, and an old past tense of crow, to boast triumphantly.

clue.text: It could well break out in Vietnam

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: Trouble is quite likely to flare up in a south-east Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break out' suggests war or disease, but describes a volcano erupting; the Sicilian one is spelt inside the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an active Sicilian volcano, liable to erupt.

clue.text: Hellenic heroine chosen by certain soldiers

indicators.note: by says the first piece stands beside the second

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president elect
the RA is the Royal Artillery, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A Greek woman of legend is picked out by a particular band of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Agamemnon's daughter in Greek tragedy, who avenges her father.

clue.text: False hair, perhaps, for the seer to fasten on

parts.note: the eye is the thing that sees, whimsically a seer
to lash something is to tie it down

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller clips on a hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seer' reads as a prophet; it is simply the organ that sees. 'for' and 'on' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these can be artificial, glued on as make-up, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Vehicle overturned in the long grass — went back over

indicators.note: in means the turned vehicle sits inside the word for the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water

indicators.note: overturned means the vehicle is read from right to left

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: A car flipped over in a meadow, and someone walked the route again to see why.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash hides the join: everything before it is wordplay. 'overturned' applies only to the vehicle, giving TRAC, and 'in' then places that within the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: followed one's steps or a route again in the other direction.

clue.text: A heavenly body of remote origin

indicators.note: of ... origin says the answer starts out from the letters of the word before, which are its source to be reworked

explanation.surface: A star or planet has come from somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin' is a loose signal that the letters of remote are the source to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shooting star, a rock burning up in the atmosphere.
